To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intracellular proton (pH) concentration is the key factor in the motility inhibition of E. coli and Salmonella by weak acids, and that the proton motive force (PMF) is not directly involved in the inhibition.
intracellular acidification by weak acids such as acetates or benzoates slows the flagellar motors of E. coli or Salmonella.
the flagellar motor of Escherichiacoli slows down and stops completely as the intracellular pH is decreased by weak acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the intracellular proton (pHi) concentration on the rotational speed of flagellar motors in E. coli and Salmonella.
the effect of weak acid and intracellular pH on the rotational speed of flagellar motors.
the effect of intracellular pH on the rotational speed of the bacterial flagellar motor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intracellular H+ concentration is a key factor that determines the rotational speed of bacterial flagellar motors.
intracellular pH is an important parameter in regulating the speed of bacterial flagellar motors.
the flagellar motor is sensitive to intracellular pH and that intracellular pH is a critical factor in regulating the speed of the flagellar motor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the flagellar motor can function at a wide range of intracellular H+ concentrations but not at a high extracellular H+ concentration.
the proton gradient is not the only driving force for the flagellar motor, and that the intracellular pH may play a role in controlling the motor function.
weak acid-mediated proton accumulation in the cells inhibits the flagellar motors by decreasing the intracellular proton motive force and by directly interfering with the torque-generating mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flagellar motors of bacteria are very sensitive to the intracellular pH.
the proton concentration inside the cell is the key determinant for the rotational speed of flagellar motors.
the flagellar motor is very sensitive to intracellular pH.
